name: Maine
$scopeNote: STATE income tax + Paid Family & Medical Leave (PFML, employee AND employer shares, contributions began 2025-01-01, benefits available from 2026-05-01). Maine has NO local income tax anywhere and NO reciprocity agreement with any state -- residents working elsewhere instead claim a RETURN-level credit for taxes paid to another jurisdiction (out of scope, same convention as every other state's return-level credit already disclosed in this project, e.g. Connecticut's).
$methodComment: See maineWithholding()'s own doc comment in src/taxes/state.ts for the full mechanism (phased standard deduction + flat per-allowance amount + progressive bracket, structurally close to Wisconsin's bracketPhaseoutDeduction() but with a genuinely different, easy-to-miss feature: Maine rounds to the nearest WHOLE DOLLAR at multiple intermediate steps, not once at the end -- confirmed against all 3 of the source document's own worked examples, reproduced exactly in tests/engine.test.ts).
exemptPretaxComment: INFERRED, not directly confirmed: Maine's own 2026 withholding instructions explicitly state 'Maine does not conform to the federal deductions that may be used to reduce the required federal withholding amount' -- but that statement is specifically about federal Form W-4 Step 4(b) (the optional itemized-deductions adjustment line), a genuinely DIFFERENT concept from whether pretax elective deferrals (401(k), section 125, etc.) reduce the wage base BEFORE withholding is computed at all. No source found this session directly addresses pretax-deferral conformity either way, so this reuses the federal-conforming exemptPretax list by inference (standard payroll practice, the same conformity pattern as Michigan/Ohio/Idaho/Connecticut/Iowa/Vermont/Massachusetts in this project) rather than PA's non-conforming empty list -- lower confidence than this project's directly-quoted conformity findings for those states.

sources.title: Maine Revenue Services -- 2025 Withholding Tables for Individual Income Tax (revised October 2024)
sources.quote: Multiply the number of withholding allowances the employee claims by $5,150 ... $12,150 ... $27,150 ... Less than $26,800 5.80% of income $26,800 but less than $63,450 $1,554 plus 6.75% ... Example 2: A single employee is paid $1,000 each week ... two withholding allowances ... Withhold $33 each week.

sources.title: U.S. Department of Labor, ETA -- Significant Provisions of State Unemployment Insurance Laws, Effective January 2025

statePaidLeaveEmployee.wageBaseComment: Maine's own statute (quoted above in maineWithholding's sources) ties the wage base to 'the annual base limit set by the U.S. Social Security Administration.' CORRECTED 2026-09-06: this was a hand-copied literal 184500 (a real, undisclosed drift risk found on a "go to every state" pass, the same anti-pattern already fixed for Washington/Connecticut/Massachusetts/Delaware's own SS-linked Paid Leave programs the same pass) -- now the 'ssWageBase' sentinel, resolved LIVE from data/federal/2026.json's own socialSecurity.wageBase by resolvePaidLeaveWageBase() in src/taxes/state.ts.

reciprocity.note: Maine has no reciprocity agreement with any state -- cross-source confirmed. Residents working elsewhere claim a return-level 'Credit for Income Tax Paid to Other Jurisdiction' instead, per Maine Revenue Services' own guide (maine.gov/revenue) -- out of scope for this per-paycheck withholding engine, same convention as every other state's return-level credit mechanism already disclosed in this project.

localTaxAbsence.$comment: CLOSED with a primary constitutional citation, on the 'fix it, find a way' pass -- upgraded from cross-source-only general knowledge.
localTaxAbsence.source: Maine Constitution, Article IX, Section 9 (Power of taxation)
localTaxAbsence.verifiedBy: Fetched directly via curl with a browser User-Agent (plain WebFetch 403s justia.com, the same pattern already documented for Vermont's law.justia.com citation). Verbatim: 'The Legislature shall never, in any manner, suspend or surrender the power of taxation.' The Legislature retains EXCLUSIVE taxing power under this provision and has never enacted legislation authorizing a municipal income tax (cross-source confirmed on this same pass, consistent with Massachusetts's own parallel finding under its Article XLIV) -- so no Maine city or town may levy one, the same two-part structure (constitutional exclusivity + no enabling legislation) already established for Massachusetts.

knownGaps: Descriptive notes carried from the 2026 file (reciprocity, local-tax rules, method comments) were checked against the 2025 source for the fields this engine computes from; narrative text that only describes 2026 history should be read as background.

verification.wholeDollarFinalRounding: CLOSED on the NFC verification pass: rules.roundFinalToWholeDollar (a new generic flag, not Maine-specific code) now re-rounds the primary SIT line to the nearest dollar AFTER additional/reduced withholding is applied, matching NFC's own Step 9 instruction exactly. Verified with a non-whole-dollar additionalWithholding test case ($33 base + $10.60 = $43.60 -> $44).
verification.pfmlSmallEmployerDiscretion: CLOSED on the 'fix it, find a way' pass: certificate.paidLeaveEmployeeRateOverride (a new generic field on the SHARED statePaidLeaveEmployeeTax(), not Maine-specific) lets a caller who knows a specific small employer's own chosen rate supply it directly, while the 0.5% default remains correct for the common case (Maine's own FAQ: 'no more than 0.5 percent can come from the employee' applies as the statutory MAXIMUM to BOTH the 15+ and under-15 tiers identically -- there was never a formula difference in the employee's own cap, only in whether the EMPLOYER'S net cost is zero or 0.5%, which this file already handles via the existing employerLiableForPaidLeaveShare gate).
verification.tribalExemptionGranularity: CLOSED on the 'fix it, find a way' pass: certificate.exemptWages (cents, this pay period) added to maineWithholding() lets a caller exclude just the tribal-land-sourced portion of wages from the taxable base, rather than the all-or-nothing certificate.exempt flag. The caller still determines eligibility and the dollar split (the same boundary as every exemption in this project) -- this only removes the previous forced choice between 'exempt the whole cheque' and 'exempt nothing' for a genuinely mixed tribal/non-tribal pay period.

suiEmployer.$comment: Normalized employer-side unemployment parameters — the shape src/taxes/state.ts reads. The detailed unemploymentInsurance block above stays the record of research; this exists because that block's shape varies too much between states to compute from directly (wage bases as objects, industry-keyed rate maps, differently-named keys).
suiEmployer.wageBaseSource: DOL Significant Provisions, January 2025 (Wages Subject to Tax)
suiEmployer.newEmployerRateSource: DOL Significant Provisions, January 2025 (New Employer Rate, base rate)

supplementalWages.source: Maine's own instructions, quoted in this file's knownGaps: aggregate if paid with regular wages; 'the payer MAY withhold a flat five percent' if paid separately. The permissive verb is why this is an election rather than a rule.

supplementalAggregation.source: Maine's instructions: aggregate if paid with regular wages; the payer MAY instead withhold a flat 5% if paid separately. Aggregation is the default this block wires.
supplementalAggregation.engineNote: Wired via aggregateWithPriorRegularPayment(): the caller supplies input.priorRegularPayment (that cheque's taxable wages and the state tax withheld from it), and a bonus paid on its own cheque is taxed on the combined figure less what was already withheld, floored at zero. Nothing changes when the caller omits it.

$yearNote: 2025 ruleset: $5,150 per allowance; withholding standard deduction $12,150 single (phased out $100,000-$175,000) / $27,150 married ($200,050-$350,050); 5.8% / 6.75% / 7.15% above $26,800 and $63,450 single, $53,600 and $126,900 married. Maine paid family and medical leave contributions (1%, up to half from the employee) began 2025-01-01, as in 2026.
